subject: research/buildbot-sheathing
professional: a construction-robotics researcher reviewing for Automation in Construction, with a wood-frame structural engineer's eye on the code inputs (APA/SDPWS/PS 2/NDS); first checks: is the joint-nail window geometry right, do the headline percentages come from the committed code, is the nearest prior work (construction tolerance analysis, automated panel lines, humanoid board installation) cited, and are the later milestones answering a question a builder has

evidence.correctness: Nine headline outputs recomputed with the auditor's own script (scratchpad recompute.py, imports nothing from the subject) from SDPWS 4.3.7.1 edge distance, 1.5 in dressed face, 0.131 in 8d shank, PS 2 diagonal rule and statics: joint half-window 3.931/3.137 mm (README 3.93/3.14), tip sigma for 95% with perfect studs 0.989 mm by closed-form erf product (MC 0.984), stud sigma for 95% at 0.9 mm tool 0.414 mm by my own Gauss-Hermite quadrature of the shared-stud model (README 0.41; clean at 0.89 mm 0.748 = README 0.748), single-2x closing bow 12.55 mm = 0.531 in 8 ft equivalent (README 0.53), PS 2 corner angle 0.0834 deg (README 0.083), push height h* = W/2mu 2.032/0.871 m (README 2.03/0.87), gravity moment 130.3 N m and 7,467 N m/rad at 1 deg (README 130 / ~7,500), butted-row sheet 3 feasibility 0.470 (results 0.46), sheet mass 21.8 kg = 1.5 psf x 32 sq ft (APA 7/16 OSB about 1.4-1.5 psf). All pass. `reproduce.py --check --quick` re-ran m1, m2, m4, m5, m7, m10, m11 (and more) in a temp copy: every results.txt line matches. Not 4: most error inputs are swept rather than measured, and the later humanoid milestones (27-60) were not recomputed independently.
evidence.completeness: Every listed milestone (1-60, minus the deliberately skipped numbers) has run.py, results.txt and figure; `reproduce.py --list` covers all 56 experiment dirs (test_reproduce asserts it). paper/draft.md is a full AutCon-format draft with highlights, abstract, LaTeX build and a 419-entry number tie-out (`python3 paper/check_numbers.py` -> 419 of 419 checks ok). Gaps: the paper covers milestones 1-24 only; m6/m6b need drake 1.51.1 (4 tests skipped here, not run); authorship and NDS/SDPWS editions are still open per paper/README.md.
evidence.verification: `/usr/bin/python3.13 -m pytest -q tests` -> 222 passed, 4 skipped (drake) in 64 s. Six hand-seeded mutations via quality_mutate.py in core logic (joint window gap/2 -> gap, minimax stud centring -> mean, edge-aim offset of 0.5 mm, plate window 7+7 -> 14 single, capital recovery factor -> 1/years, hand-crew minutes/60 -> /50): all six caught. reproduce.py --check diffs every non-timing results line against the committed file (m3_ledger with MuJoCo 3.x also re-run). Tests compare against closed forms (erf products, translation/rotation limits, PS 2 geometry), not only snapshots. Kept at 3 rather than 4 because the 30 humanoid milestones' planners were not mutated and their tests largely check internal consistency.
evidence.craft: Read src/buildbot_sheathing/budget.py, asbuilt.py (simulate, max_feasible_bow), ledger.py (corner_angle_limit), cost.py (crf, hand_cost), reproduce.py, experiments/m60_jointpreload/core.py. Library code is vectorised, documented with units and sources, and tested. Defects: experiments chain by importing each other's run.py by file path 20 deep (m60 core.py -> m59 -> ... -> m38), so a change to an old experiment script silently changes every later milestone; the project imports three sibling projects via pyproject pythonpath; README is 2,093 lines with headline, method and results sections for 60 milestones.
evidence.claims: Checked: the 62-nail schedule (34+14+14, test_budget), 3.14 mm window, 87% single-2x cap (m2 results 0.8685), 99.94% doubled joints single read (m5 results line 19/85), 37% beat-the-crew (m7), 21.8 kg, h*, PS 2 limits; all backed by committed results and the paper tie-out. Sources are marked honestly ('seen in search, not opened', 'from memory', 'not sourced'), limitations are long and specific, AI assistance and 'nothing tested on hardware' are on the README and the served page (marisstella.app/research/buildbot-sheathing/ HTTP 200, current to milestone 60). Misses: highlight and abstract give 99.94% for doubled joints with one read without saying it is the lower published warp (higher warp single read 0.9404, m5 results:86, absent from the paper); paper/README.md says check_numbers prints 194 of 194 (now 419).
evidence.fitness: A researcher could build on it: one command reproduces each experiment, the error model is explicit and the code is MIT. Nearest prior work checked: Kumagai et al. 2019 (HRP-5P plasterboard), Adel et al. 2024 AutCon, Cote et al. 2024 Construction Robotics, Willmann 2016 are cited and real (Crossref confirms DOIs). Missing: construction dimensional-tolerance analysis in the target venue itself (Rausch, Nahangi, Haas and West 2017, AutCon 75:33-44, doi:10.1016/j.autcon.2016.12.001; Milberg and Tommelein 2005 tolerance mapping, doi:10.1061/40754(183)113), and the industrial baseline: wall-panel lines with multifunction nailing bridges already sheathe walls automatically, so the 'gantry' class is priced from an unsourced $40k-600k sweep instead of vendor data. The core result (joint framing, not sensing, sets the clean-sheet rate) is new and sound as a tolerance allocation; milestones 41-60 then spend twenty milestones driving a humanoid tool-point residual under an unsourced 0.03 mm 'spec' (30x below the 0.9 mm tool scatter the budget assumes), each on one seed, statics only, which a reviewer would cut.
evidence.domain: Compared against SDPWS 4.3.7.1 (3/8 in panel-edge distance, 3x or two 2x at adjoining edges), APA 1/8 in gap, PS 2-18 squareness (1/64 in/ft diagonals) and straightness, 8d common 0.131 x 2.5 in, IRC 6/12 in schedule: the window geometry and inputs match. Departures: the 10D penetration rule (README.md:848, 'from memory') is the pre-2005 NDS penetration-factor rule; current NDS has a 6D minimum with yield equations using actual penetration, and the 10D figure drives the twist band and m29/m59's 44.4 mm depth point (6D is swept, which mitigates). Treating any single shiner as a failed sheet is stricter than field practice (re-nailing), disclosed. Capacity models (m14-m21) use NDS design-level ratios against tested ultimates, disclosed.

defects.what: Related work and the novelty claim ('No work we found propagates the full chain ...') omit the nearest prior work in the target venue: dimensional-variation / tolerance analysis of construction assemblies (Rausch, Nahangi, Haas and West 2017, Automation in Construction 75:33-44; Milberg and Tommelein 2005 tolerance mapping) and the industrial baseline of automated wall-panel lines with multifunction nailing bridges, which already sheathe walls; the gantry class is priced from an unsourced $40k-600k sweep instead

Milestones 41-60 optimise a humanoid's tool-point residual against a 0.03 mm 'spec' that no source gives (the z and depth specs are the y figure 'carried over, not sourced'), 30 times below the 0.9 mm tool scatter the clean-sheet budget assumes, each milestone on one seed and statics only; twenty milestones of planner tuning against a self-set target that is never tied back to the clean-sheet rate a builder inspects

Highlight and abstract state doubled joint studs give 99.94% clean sheets with one read a stud without saying this is the lower published warp; at the higher published warp the same policy gives 0.9404 (m5 results line 86), a figure the paper never reports. Small safe fix: add 'at the lower published stud warp (94% at the higher)'

Required penetration of 10 nail diameters is cited as the 'NDS full-design-value penetration, from memory'; that is the pre-2005 NDS penetration-factor rule (current NDS: 6D minimum, yield equations with actual penetration). It is the default of the twist band and the 44.4 mm depth point of milestones 29 and 59; 6D is swept
paper/README.md says check_numbers.py prints '194 of 194 checks ok'; it now prints 419 of 419. Small safe fix

Experiments import earlier experiments' run.py by file path in a chain 20 deep (m60 core.py -> m59 -> ... -> m38), so editing any old experiment script silently changes every later milestone's model; the shared planner belongs in src/ with tests

The milestone 7 cost headline (G1 on a base beats a crew in 37% of draws; gantry cheaper only above ~500 houses a year) is driven most by inputs the README marks unsourced (base price, life, interest, gantry price; rank correlation +-0.58)

verdict: A serious, reproducible tolerance-allocation programme: every headline geometry and statics number I recomputed from SDPWS/APA/PS 2 inputs and my own quadrature matched (9 of 9), 222 tests pass, six seeded bugs in core logic were all caught, and reproduce.py re-creates the committed results line for line. The central finding, that doubled joint framing rather than sensing sets the clean-sheet rate on bowed studs, is sound and likely publishable as a narrow AutCon tolerance paper. It falls short of expert grade on research design: the related work misses construction tolerance analysis in the target venue and the industrial nail-bridge baseline, the abstract's 99.94% hides the 94% at the higher published warp, and the last twenty milestones tune a humanoid planner against an unsourced 0.03 mm target on one seed each. Meets the bar on correctness, claims and verification; fitness is the weak dimension.
